topic_tag: a drought and a pine forest
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Reading the tree rings decades later, one forest ecologist concluded that the drought had ______ the pines on the ridge.

worlds.passage: For centuries pines have covered a dry foothill ridge, with a few scrub oaks scattered among them, and in the 1950s a seven-year drought struck it. Nearly every pine has a ring for each year of the drought, hair-thin, and the rings of every decade since are barely wider. Pines that sprouted on the ridge in the 1940s now stand about half as tall as pines of the same age on a wetter slope across the valley, and their crowns still close over the scattered oaks. Reading the tree rings decades later, one forest ecologist concluded that the drought had ______ the pines on the ridge.
worlds.explanation: The pines survived, but their growth never recovered and they are half the height of pines the same age elsewhere: the drought "stunted" them. "Toughened" fails because the passage records lasting damage, not new hardiness; "thinned" fails because nearly every pine has a ring for each drought year, so they survived; "sidelined" fails because their crowns still close over the oaks.

toughened.quote: about half as tall as pines of the same age
toughened.why: The record is of lasting harm; nothing shows the pines became hardier.

thinned.quote: Nearly every pine has a ring for each year
thinned.why: Trees that laid down rings throughout the drought survived it, so the stand was not made sparser.

sidelined.quote: their crowns still close over the scattered oaks
sidelined.why: The pines kept their dominant place.

worlds.passage: For centuries pines have covered a dry foothill ridge, with a few scrub oaks scattered among them, and in the 1950s a seven-year drought struck it. During the drought the rings narrowed sharply, and within five years they had widened to their old breadth again. When dry years returned in the 1970s, the ridge pines laid down rings almost as wide as in a wet year, while pines on a wetter slope across the valley, which had never known drought, laid down their narrowest rings on record. Reading the tree rings decades later, one forest ecologist concluded that the drought had ______ the pines on the ridge.
worlds.explanation: In the next drought, the pines that had been through the 1950s grew almost normally while untested pines nearby barely grew, so the drought made them hardier: it "toughened" them. "Stunted" fails because their rings widened to their old breadth; "thinned" fails because the same trees are tracked through the 1970s; "sidelined" fails because they kept growing strongly.

stunted.quote: widened to their old breadth again
stunted.why: Growth that fully recovered was not permanently held back.

thinned.quote: the ridge pines laid down rings
thinned.why: The account follows the pines as a surviving stand; nothing indicates many died.

sidelined.quote: almost as wide as in a wet year
sidelined.why: Pines growing strongly in a dry spell were not pushed out of their place.

worlds.passage: For centuries pines have covered a dry foothill ridge, with a few scrub oaks scattered among them, and in the 1950s a seven-year drought struck it. Stumps and fallen trunks dating from the drought years lie all across the ridge, about one for every two living pines, mostly small trees that had grown crowded together. The surviving pines, with more water and light to share, laid down wider rings after the drought than before it, and they still make up nearly all of the canopy. Reading the tree rings decades later, one forest ecologist concluded that the drought had ______ the pines on the ridge.
worlds.explanation: About a third of the pines died, mostly crowded small ones, leaving survivors with more room: the drought "thinned" them. "Stunted" fails because the survivors grew wider rings afterward; "toughened" fails because their gain came from having more water and light to share, not from hardiness; "sidelined" fails because pines still make up nearly all of the canopy.

stunted.quote: wider rings after the drought than before
stunted.why: Growth that improved was not held back.

toughened.quote: with more water and light to share
toughened.why: Their better growth came from less crowding, not from greater hardiness.

sidelined.why: The pines kept their dominant place.

worlds.passage: For centuries pines have covered a dry foothill ridge, with a few scrub oaks scattered among them, and in the 1950s a seven-year drought struck it. Nearly every pine came through the drought, and their rings returned to normal breadth within a few years. The oaks, which draw on water far below the pines' roots, kept growing through the dry years, and today their crowns spread above the pines across most of the ridge, while the seedlings on the ground beneath are nearly all oak. Reading the tree rings decades later, one forest ecologist concluded that the drought had ______ the pines on the ridge.
worlds.explanation: The oaks grew through the drought and now overtop the pines, with oak seedlings taking over beneath, so the pines lost their dominant place: the drought "sidelined" them. "Stunted" fails because the pines' rings returned to normal; "toughened" fails because nothing shows them coping better with drought; "thinned" fails because nearly every pine survived.

stunted.why: Growth that fully recovered was not permanently held back.

toughened.quote: seedlings on the ground beneath are nearly all oak
toughened.why: The outcome is the pines losing ground, not gaining hardiness.

thinned.why: Few pines died, so the stand was not made sparser.
